content.comment_body: Hello, I previously used a [version_no] PLC to read pulses generated by an inductive sensor (BALLUFF BES517-223-M5-E), and everything worked fine. The sensor uses two wires, and the entire system operates at 110VAC with a low frequency (around 1Hz). I'm now trying to use the same setup, but with a recently purchased [product_name] ([version_no]). When I connected the sensor, I wasn't getting any pulses. After reading the manual, I saw mention of using a capacitor or resistor. Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you.

The capacitor referenced in the manual is only applicable for switches that include a glow lamp as an indicator. 2-wire proximity switches always maintain a minimum current, even when no object is detected. For some of these switches, the residual current is high enough that the input of the [product_name] registers this as an active signal.
Hello, thank you for your response. I was able to find a capacitor (470nF), and the sensor started working!

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered a compatibility issue when switching from a [version_no] PLC to a [product_name] ([version_no]) in an application with a 2-wire inductive sensor (BALLUFF BES517-223-M5-E). The initial sensor setup did not function until a capacitor was added, resolving the issue. The challenge arose because the [product_name] input could potentially interpret residual current from the sensor as an active signal, a nuance not always evident when transitioning from more advanced PLC models.
